question: Can graph neural-network layers across spatial, attention, spectral, transformer, heterogeneous, higher-order, and geometric families be normalized into one checkable equation that supports coverage, comparison, theoretical attribution, and disciplined architecture generation?

key_findings.claim: A seven-slot layer equation captures a broad range of GNN computations while keeping routing and message content explicitly separate.
key_findings.evidence: The layer specifies updated domain, channel set, propagation operators, message maps, fusion, ego/residual path, and final update. Exact reductions are given for GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, and GIN; MPNN is an exact node-domain specialization, while a full Graph Network block requires staged typed updates. Graded extensions cover node-edge, tuple, subgraph, cell, and equivariant settings.

key_findings.claim: Raw channel count is not an identifiable measure of architectural complexity in the linear additive regime.
key_findings.evidence: Channels can be split or canceled without changing the layer map. For T(H)=sum_k P_k H W_k, the invariant is the minimum Kronecker separation rank of vec(T)=sum_k (W_k^T tensor P_k), not the syntactic number of terms.

key_findings.claim: Several familiar GNN phenomena become slot-conditional statements rather than architecture-name-level explanations.
key_findings.evidence: Under positive-homogeneous 1-Lipschitz message/update maps, one layer contracts Dirichlet energy by at most (s mu*)^2; an initial residual yields a nonzero anchor-dependent energy floor. Local endpoint messages and node-local updates bound one-layer dependency support, while one-layer global mixing with fixed operators requires a full effective off-diagonal row; a synchronous virtual node takes two layers to relay information globally.

key_findings.claim: The factorization supports constrained architecture proposals, but the paper does not test whether those proposals work.
key_findings.evidence: An LLM controller generated six typed candidates—spectrally gated, relation-equivariant, subgraph-attentive, spectral-biased transformer, curvature-gated, and sequential co-lifted node-edge layers—which were audited for domains, dimensions, symmetry, and execution order. The authors explicitly present them as auditable candidates rather than empirical improvements.

key_findings.claim: The framework is descriptive and diagnostic; it does not solve the inverse problem of choosing the best slots for a dataset.
key_findings.evidence: Benchmark mappings are labeled descriptive rather than causal attribution, and the conclusion states that selecting an architecture from desired properties remains an empirical inverse problem. Open problems include dense-attention scaling, temporal memory, readout, graph foundation models, trust, retrieval, and evaluation design.

method.core_idea: Normalize a GNN layer into typed computational slots so apparently different architectures can be compared by what domain they update, where information travels, what message is sent, how channels fuse, and how ego information enters.
method.mechanism: For each channel, a propagation bank P_k defines routing and a message map Psi_k defines values; a fusion operator combines channels, B_l carries an ego or residual contribution, and phi_l updates the selected domain. Pairwise messages handle state-dependent neighbor interactions, and rectangular inter-rank operators extend the equation to graded domains. Slot-level assumptions then yield permutation-equivariance, support, smoothing, polynomial-filter, expressivity, and globality statements.
assumptions: Architectures can be expressed under the paper's fixed slot discipline without hiding decisive computation inside an unrestricted message or update map.
Theoretical consequences invoke their stated regimes, including fixed operators, locality, linear additive channels, Lipschitz maps, or synchronous execution.
Family assignments are nonexclusive and use a subjective primary-axis convention.
Layer-level normalization is useful even though pooling, training objectives, temporal state, and full model topology may lie outside the base equation.

techniques.role: Separates where information travels from what values are transmitted, preventing routing and content from being conflated.
Maps layers to updated domain, channels, propagation, messages, fusion, ego path, and update for checkable comparisons.
Uses rectangular inter-rank operators and typed scheduling to cover nodes, edges, tuples, subgraphs, and cells.
Replaces non-identifiable raw channel count with the minimum separable operator-message rank in linear additive layers.
Derives receptive-field and global-mixing limits from propagation support and local update assumptions.
Checks generated architectures for type, dimension, symmetry, and execution validity before empirical testing.

evaluations.setting: Canonical GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, and GIN layers
evaluations.metric: Exact symbolic reduction into the seven slots
evaluations.result: All four are represented exactly with explicit choices of propagation, message, fusion, ego, and update
MPNN is an exact node-domain specialization; the node-update slice of a Graph Network is covered, while the full edge-node-global block needs staged typed updates
evaluations.baseline: Original MPNN and Graph Network equations

evaluations.setting: Survey mapping across seven nonexclusive GNN families
evaluations.result: More than 200 architectures are mapped in comparison tables

evaluations.metric: Type, dimension, permutation/symmetry, and execution-order audit
evaluations.result: Six internally checkable candidate equations are produced; no accuracy or efficiency results are reported
Equivalent split and cancel constructions show channel count is not identifiable; minimum Kronecker separation rank is invariant
Global mixing requires full effective off-diagonal row support; a virtual node relays globally only after two synchronous layers
evaluations.baseline: Informal claims that a virtual node is immediately global

limitations: Author-stated: generated architectures are hypotheses and receive no empirical performance evaluation.
Author-stated: benchmark translations are descriptive and do not establish causal attribution to individual slots.
Author-stated: the base layer excludes or needs extensions for pooling/readout, staged full Graph Network blocks, temporal memory, and some sorting, search, embedding, or nested-GNN mechanisms.
Author-stated: choosing slot values from a desired task property remains an unsolved inverse problem.

Reviewer-identified: many theoretical statements specialize established equivariance, smoothing, locality, polynomial-filter, and WL results; the principal novelty is the factorization and synthesis rather than wholly new GNN theory.
Reviewer-identified: an unrestricted Psi or phi can absorb computation and make nominally different slot assignments computationally equivalent, limiting taxonomy determinacy.
Reviewer-identified: coverage counts and primary-family labels depend on curatorial judgment and do not demonstrate that the schema improves search, reproducibility, or model selection.
failure_modes: A model may fit the equation only by hiding its distinctive computation inside a generic message map, making the comparison vacuous.
Ignoring execution order can falsely claim coverage of edge-node-global or co-lifted updates that are not simultaneous.
Support and globality conclusions fail for globally state-dependent propagation operators or nonlocal updates.
Linear additive identifiability results do not transfer directly to nonlinear attention, gating, normalization, or multiplicative fusion.
Slot-by-slot ablations can misattribute performance when propagation, message, normalization, residual, and training choices interact.
A type-correct generated architecture can still be statistically weak, computationally infeasible, or redundant with an existing model.
reusable_insights: Document graph layers by routing, values, fusion, ego path, update, and domain rather than by architecture name alone.
State the execution schedule whenever multiple entity ranks update; algebraic notation without timing can conceal a different model.
Use invariant functional rank instead of raw branch count when comparing linear multichannel layers.
Attach every theoretical diagnosis to the exact slot assumptions under which it holds.
Treat architecture generation as constrained program synthesis: first type- and symmetry-check candidates, then benchmark them.
Translate benchmarks into required locality, symmetry, relation, and scale properties before selecting model families, while keeping the final choice empirical.
open_questions: Can task and graph statistics reliably predict slot choices before expensive hyperparameter search?
Which slot representations remain identifiable under nonlinear, input-dependent, and multiplicative interactions?
Does slot-normalized reporting improve reproducibility or causal architecture attribution in controlled benchmarks?
How should pooling, global state, temporal memory, retrieval, and graph-agent actions be incorporated without making the equation universal but uninformative?
Can generated candidates be deduplicated by functional equivalence and ranked by compute before training?
What empirical evidence would show that the common equation is a useful search space rather than only a survey notation?

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
competitive_landscape.difference: Gilmer et al. unified molecular graph models as message-passing neural networks with message and update phases. The new paper refines that view with explicit propagation-versus-value factorization, multiple channels, fusion, ego paths, identifiability, and graded domains across a wider GNN landscape.

competitive_landscape.title: Relational inductive biases, deep learning, and graph networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Battaglia et al.'s Graph Network block is broader at the full-model level because it stages edge, node, and global updates. The common equation is finer-grained for one layer's routing and message roles, but covers the full GN block only through its typed staged extension.

competitive_landscape.title: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
competitive_landscape.difference: Geometric Deep Learning provides a broader symmetry- and domain-based blueprint spanning grids, manifolds, groups, and graphs. This paper is narrower but more operational: it gives a slot-level GNN equation, exact reductions, functional identifiability, and auditable generation rules.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the paper unifies more than 200 GNN layers through a common equation whose explicit operator-message separation supports comparison, theory, and architecture generation. Reviewer inference: MPNN, Graph Networks, and Geometric Deep Learning already provide influential unifying languages. The most defensible increment is the unusually explicit seven-slot normalization—especially separating routing from values, adding graded domains, and identifying Kronecker separation rank—plus a large source-grounded atlas. Because no generated model is tested and benchmark mappings are noncausal, claims that the framework enables better architecture design remain prospective.
reviewer_notes: The full survey, theory, comparison tables, proofs, and appendices were reviewed. Theoretical and quantitative statements were checked at their cited pages. Primary arXiv records were used for all three predecessor frameworks. The novelty judgment distinguishes representational synthesis from new empirical architecture results.
